title: Identification with continuous étale cohomology
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\Sh(X_{\Et})^{\mathbf N}$ be the abelian category of
inverse systems $(G_n)_{n\geq1}$ of abelian étale sheaves, and let
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}((G_n))=\Gamma(X_{\Et},\varprojlim_nG_n)=
\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X_{\Et},G_n)$. For an inverse system $(F_{n,\Et})$ with
epimorphic transitions and $F_n=\nu_X^*F_{n,\Et}$,

$$
R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cont}}((F_{n,\Et}))\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_{n,\Et})
\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(X_{\Proet},F_n)\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\Proet},\varprojlim_nF_n).
$$

proof.text: Abelian etale sheaves form a Grothendieck category. Prove the same for its tower category: the evaluation left adjoints applied to a separator form a small separating family; their coproduct is a separator, filtered colimits and AB5 are levelwise, and natural transformations are a subtype of a small family of component morphisms. Hence every tower complex has a K-injective resolution. Continuous sections are the additive functor lim composed with levelwise global sections. The functor-equivalence between complexes of towers and towers of complexes, together with the degreewise-limit isomorphism, identifies its map on complexes with continuousEtaleSectionComplexes. Use the existing K-injective right derivability structure and rightDerivedFunctorUnit, whiskered with the homotopy quotient comparisons, to obtain a right derived functor of this exact complex functor, whose unit is invertible on every K-injective complex. All choices are of universal derived-functor data, not arbitrary existence witnesses.

source.place: Tags 0940, 0941, 07A5; K-injective derivability for continuous sections

proof.text: Levelwise constant sheaves are an exact left adjoint to levelwise sections, by whiskering the ordinary adjunction and using finite-limit preservation of sheafification. The sections tower functor therefore preserves K-injectivity. Resolve F[0] by a K-injective complex I of etale towers. Evaluation preserves quasi-isomorphisms and K-injectivity, so the derived unit at every evaluated complex identifies its section complex with RGamma(F_n[0]), naturally in every transition. The generic derivedCategory_towerLimit_property applied to the section tower gives its termwise limit the required Roos triangle. The unit of Rc at I and Rc applied to the resolution identify Rc(F[0]) with that same complex. Transport the distinguished triangle along this isomorphism. This gives L1 = Rc(F[0]) and the first derived-limit assertion without the epimorphic assumption.

The exact comparison inverse image preserves epimorphisms. Apply the source-library bounded-below comparison unit to each degree-zero etale sheaf; the generic coefficient theorem specializes directly to AddCommGrpCat, using its tensor monoidal and functorial flat-resolution instances. Whisker that unit with derived etale sections and use comparisonLowerStarCompRightDerivedGlobalSectionsIso and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor. This produces a natural isomorphism of the sheaf-to-derived-sections functors, hence an isomorphism of the two original towers, with the specified transition maps. Transport a Roos triangle along the induced isomorphism of products to obtain a pro-etale derived-limit structure on L1.

source.place: Tags 099V and 099W; the comparison on degree-zero sheaves

proof.text: Compute the pro-etale Roos limit directly for abelian sheaves. Over a weakly contractible affine covering family, every epimorphic transition is surjective on sections. Given y in the product, choose x_0=0 and lift x_n-y_n to x_(n+1); this proves surjectivity of 1-shift on sections of each covering object and hence epimorphy as a sheaf map. Repleteness supplies exact countable products of abelian sheaves via CountableAB4Star.of_epi_pi_app_zero. The ordinary inverse limit is the kernel of 1-shift, so its short exact Roos sequence yields a distinguished triangle under the degree-zero embedding. That embedding preserves the countable product: the single-complex functor does, and the localization Q does when products are exact. Derived global sections are a triangulated right adjoint, by the exact constant-sheaf adjunction, so they preserve this homotopy-limit cone. Transfer from its chosen product to the product in IsDerivedLimit. Thus L2 = RGamma((lim nu^*F)[0]) is a derived limit of the pulled-back section tower.

source.place: Bhatt--Scholze Propositions 3.1.9, 3.1.10, 4.2.8, 5.6.2; local recursive proof of the Roos epimorphism

proof.text: Use exact products of abelian groups to obtain countable products in D(Ab). Both L1, after tower transport, and L2 are derived limits of exactly the same pro-etale tower. Apply exists_isDerivedLimit_and_iso for their isomorphism. The first and last displayed isomorphisms are identities by the chosen L1 and L2. This proves all clauses of the unchanged theorem.
